support: Partner preview: best-effort support, no production commitment. Frozen fields in the pinned component files are the contract; a breaking change to a documented surface opens a new Distribution line, announced in advance.

surfaces._note: First point on the phoenix line: every surface is new; there is no previous point to diff against. From the next cut on, this block reports what changed per surface, derived from machine diffs of the pinned ABIs and schemas.

integrationSuite.decision: No cross-component integration suite exists for this first cut; waived by the distribution owner (2026-08-07). The Distribution therefore keeps its candidate (-rc) name.
integrationSuite.nearestEvidence: cork-cli fork-proven end-to-end (reads, derivations, JIT order building, oracle deploy path, settlement through the real 1inch Limit Order Protocol on a Base fork) against phoenix v1.3.0-rc.1 and the market-registry generation preceding 0.3.3 (2026-08-10). 0.3.3 is an interface-identical redeployment of that generation; live quickstart command runs were re-verified against chain.

externalDependencies._note: Third-party contracts the pinned set calls into. Not Cork components, but an integrator's threat model includes them, so the pin records exactly which ones this set was built against.

deterministic-deployment-factory.note: CREATE2 address identity across chains depends on this factory.

announcements: GitHub Releases on each pinned repository are the notice channel for cuts, deprecations and removals.
knownIssues: Rollover is not part of this Distribution.
Admin and operational timelocks run at a 0-second delay — a documented fact of this partner-preview deployment.
scopeNotes: The registry read API is not part of this Distribution: nothing in the partner integration path calls it — the CLI/MCP tool reads the registry directly from chain. It joins a later Distribution.
Naming: a Distribution line is named after its main component — this is the phoenix line.
